verdict.evidence:
Paste builds each new edge id from node ids only, ignoring handles, so two copied parallel edges between the same node pair collide.

useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:109-114 (paste):
  const newEdges = copiedEdges.flatMap((ed) => {
    const newSource = idMap.get(ed.source); const newTarget = idMap.get(ed.target)
    if (!newSource || !newTarget) return []
    return [{ ...ed, id: `e-${newSource}-${newTarget}`, source: newSource, target: newTarget }]
  })
The id depends solely on (newSource, newTarget); sourceHandle/targetHandle ride along via ...ed but never enter the id.

Parallel edges between one node pair ARE legal and the codebase keys ids on handles precisely for this:
- flowElements.ts:76-89 edgeId() = ["e", source, target, targetHandle||"default", sourceHandle||"default"].join("_") — canonical builder folds BOTH handles in.
- useEdgeHandlers.ts:138-144 duplicate guard uniqueness key = (source, target, sourceHandle, targetHandle); edges differing only in a handle are NOT duplicates and both persist.

Concrete reachable instance: apiInput nodes expose multiple distinct source handles (apiInputPorts.ts:99-112), and a POLARS target has no maxInputs cap (nodeTypes.ts:66; wouldExceedMaxInputs returns false when meta.maxInputs is unset, useEdgeHandlers.ts:44-47). Two edges apiInput->polars on sourceHandle "tableA" vs "tableB" (both targetHandle null via normalizeDefaultTargetHandle, flowHandles.ts:3-5) coexist with distinct canonical ids e_apiInput_polars_default_tableA / _tableB. Copy captures both (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:72-75 internalEdges = both endpoints selected); paste maps both to the same `e-${newSource}-${newTarget}` => identical id. React Flow requires unique edge ids, so one pasted edge is dropped / mis-rendered — a silent connection loss in the pasted subgraph (originals untouched).

Nuance: the description's cited edgeJoin example (base/join role handles "both fed from copies of the same upstream node") is actually NOT constructable — insertEdgeJoinNode/insertEdgeJoinNodeFromSources reject same-source-into-both-handles via the self-join guard (edgeJoinGraph.ts:84,141). But the claim does not depend on that case; the apiInput multi-port / differing-sourceHandle path proves the collision.
verdict.recommended_fix: In useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:113, build the pasted edge id with the canonical builder so handles are included: import edgeId from utils/flowElements and use `id: edgeId(newSource, newTarget, ed.targetHandle, ed.sourceHandle)`. Add a TDD test: copy an apiInput + downstream Polars connected by two ports, paste, assert the two new edges have distinct ids and both survive.
